title: Repeated increments preserve bounded reachability
statement: Let $A$ be an arithmetic register program, let $x$ be a Boolean input, and let $r$ be one of its registers. Suppose $k,B\in\mathbb{N}$, the instruction at each of the states $\ell_0,\ldots,\ell_{k-1}$ increments register $r$ and proceeds to the next state, and an initial register valuation $v$ satisfies $v(s)\le B$ for every register $s$ and $v(r)+k\le B$. Then the program can reach the configuration with state $\ell_k$, register valuation obtained by replacing $v(r)$ with $v(r)+k$, and no answer yet, from the configuration with state $\ell_0$, valuation $v$, and no answer yet, with the precondition holding at every preceding step and all register values bounded by $B$.
hypotheses_covered: Arithmetic register program, oracle, Boolean input, and register $r$
Each of the first $k$ state instructions increments $r$ and advances to the next state
Every initial register value is at most $B$
The initial value of $r$ plus $k$ is at most $B$
